facts: NBS Circular 592 reports that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels (types 316 and 317) were the most resistant at low temperatures.
NBS Circular 592 reports that at about 150°F all of the stainless steels corrode in practically all concentrations of acid up to 95%.

NBS Circular 592 reports Roach and Hall stated that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels (316/317) were useful, at room temperature, in sulfuric acid concentrations below about 15% and above about 85%.

Therefore, stainless steels should not be treated generically as acceptable for sulfuric acid service at ≈150°F; screening should mark stainless steels as potentially unsuitable and require alloy-specific compatibility data or corrosion testing before approval.
